title: Vector-Symbolic Intelligence in Practice
lines: Vector-Symbolic Intelligence in Practice reports what survived inspection of an experimental research programme.
Fifteen repository snapshots were examined through code reading, selected reruns, and diagnostic experiments.
The book separates mathematical limitations from decoder errors, software defects, and unsuitable tests.
Its value is the connection between ambitious representations and evidence that can challenge them.
This is an experimental record, rather than proof of a finished language-model alternative.

title: What a passing test establishes
lines: A successful test suite may measure a narrower ability than its surrounding description suggests.
The book follows code, operators, representations, and evaluation assumptions together.
Preserving an index is different from understanding the roles inside an event.
A role-order collision therefore matters differently from a missing software dependency.
These distinctions make the experimental record more informative than an impressive total of passed tests.

title: Change the explanation of failure
lines: In one tested linear setting, a different readout removed the observed decoding error.
That result narrows one failure claim without solving every representation problem.
Other experiments trade holographic interference for explicit storage growth.
The book counts those costs instead of treating exactness as free.
Its comparisons keep the required operation visible when judging an architecture.

title: Read the reversible conclusions
lines: Begin with the code-inspection chapter before interpreting the individual experimental results.
Follow the cases that distinguish representation limits from errors elsewhere in the system.
The conclusions identify candidate contributions and experiments that could reverse the current assessment.
This book is useful as an auditable research journey with incomplete results.
Read it to understand what these architectures have demonstrated, and what still needs testing.
